title: H517: OPT-based LLM sentiment scoring as FinBERT upgrade in H174 PEAD pipeline
rationale: arXiv:2412.19245 'Sentiment Trading with Large Language Models' (Kirtac & Germano) benchmarks FinBERT, BERT, OPT, and the Loughran-McDonald dictionary on 965,375 US financial news articles 2010-2023 for next-day return prediction. OPT scored highest on both classification accuracy (74.4% vs FinBERT's 72.2%) and long-short strategy Sharpe ratio (3.05 vs FinBERT's 2.07) -- a 47% Sharpe improvement over the exact model H163/H174 currently use. This is a distinct upgrade path from the already-staged H465 (FinDPO continuous scoring, arXiv:2507.18417): FinDPO targets calibration (continuous vs binary scores), OPT targets raw signal quality (a different base model architecture scoring higher on the same sentiment-classification task). Verified via grep this is not yet covered anywhere in wiki/ or dream_cycle/ (checked '2412.19245', 'Kirtac', and 'OPT' sentiment specifically). Caveat: the paper's dataset is general financial news, not EDGAR 8-K press releases specifically -- H163/H174's domain (post-earnings 8-K text) is narrower, so transfer needs validation on the same OOS event set before treating the paper's Sharpe as directly comparable.

hypothesis_log_entry.title: OPT LLM Sentiment Scoring Upgrade for H174 PEAD Pipeline
hypothesis_log_entry.source: arXiv:2412.19245 (Kirtac & Germano, 'Sentiment Trading with Large Language Models')
hypothesis_log_entry.mechanism: OPT (open pretrained transformer) sentiment scores on financial news text outperform FinBERT on both classification accuracy (74.4% vs 72.2%) and long-short strategy Sharpe (3.05 vs 2.07) in the source paper's general-news benchmark. If this generalizes to EDGAR 8-K press-release text, swapping H163/H174's FinBERT scorer for an OPT-based scorer (or ensembling both) could lift OOS WR/MeanRet beyond H174's confirmed 81.8%/6.89% baseline.

variants.A: OPT sentiment score alone, same 0.18-equivalent threshold re-calibrated to OPT's score distribution
variants.B: OPT score replacing FinBERT in H174's dual filter (OPT >= threshold AND surprise >= 0.02)
variants.C: FinBERT x OPT ensemble (product or average of both scores)
variants.D: OPT score >= threshold AND FinDPO score >= 0.50 (if H465 has been run by this point, three-way comparison)

design.gate: OOS WR > 81.8% AND mean_ret > 6.89% AND n >= 20 events (same H174 gate)

implementation_notes: OPT model needs to be pulled from HuggingFace -- verify exact model name/checkpoint used by the paper before install (hallusquatting defense per standing instructions)
Run pip-audit after installing any new model package
Evaluate on same H174 OOS event set (21+ confirmable events) for direct comparison
Paper's Sharpe numbers come from general financial news, not 8-K earnings press releases -- do not assume the 3.05 Sharpe transfers; treat as a reason to test, not a result to cite
If both H465 (FinDPO) and H517 (OPT) get built, run a single 3-way bake-off (FinBERT baseline vs FinDPO vs OPT) rather than two separate isolated backtests
hypothesis_log_entry.priority: MEDIUM -- alternative LLM-upgrade path alongside H465; only H163/H174-family upgrade with a directly comparable Sharpe delta reported in source literature
hypothesis_log_entry.prior_art: H174 CONFIRMED; H163 CONFIRMED (FinBERT baseline); H465 PROPOSED (FinDPO continuous scoring, complementary not competing upgrade); H168 NOT CONFIRMED (speaker-weighted FinBERT); H317 NOT CONFIRMED (FinBERT + EPS filter reduces n below gate)
